evals.name: readert-over-transformer-stack
evals.prompt: I'm structuring a web service in Haskell. My application monad is currently `newtype App a = App (ExceptT AppError (StateT AppState (ReaderT AppEnv IO)) a)`. I use StateT for a request counter and some in-memory caches, and ExceptT for domain errors. Is this a good design, and if not how should I structure the app monad?
evals.expected_output: Recommends a newtype over ReaderT Env IO instead of a deep transformer stack; replace StateT with an IORef/TVar held in the environment; drop ExceptT and throw exceptions in IO, catching at boundaries; the env should hold resources (pools, loggers, config), not mutable business state. Bonus: Has-pattern / least-context MonadReader constraints, runApp unwrap.
assertions: Recommends a newtype over `ReaderT Env IO` rather than a deep transformer stack
Says to replace StateT with an IORef/TVar held in the environment, not StateT in the stack
Says to drop ExceptT and throw exceptions in IO, catching at boundaries
Notes the environment should hold resources (pools, loggers, config), not mutable business state
Bonus: mentions the Has-pattern / polymorphic MonadReader constraints for least-context functions

evals.name: make-illegal-states-unrepresentable
evals.prompt: Here's a type I'm using in production: `data User = User { userRole :: String, userEmail :: String, userId :: Int64 }`. Roles are only ever "admin", "editor", or "viewer", and emails must contain an @. How would an experienced Haskeller improve this type?
evals.expected_output: Replace the stringly-typed role with a sum type (Admin | Editor | Viewer); wrap email in a newtype with a smart constructor that validates; use a newtype for the identifier (UserId) so it can't be confused with other Int64 ids; strict fields. Bonus: type-prefixed field names to avoid global record-name clashes, DerivingStrategies.
assertions: Replaces the stringly-typed role with a sum type (e.g. data Role = Admin | Editor | Viewer)
Wraps the email in a newtype with a smart constructor that validates the invariant
Prefers a simple Either String error for the smart constructor over a bespoke error ADT (typed errors only when matched on for flow control)
Uses a newtype for the identifier (e.g. UserId) to prevent mixing it with other Int64 ids
Recommends strict fields (!) on the record
Bonus: type-prefixed field names to avoid global name clashes, and/or explicit DerivingStrategies

evals.name: foldl-space-leak
evals.prompt: My Haskell batch job runs out of memory while summing a few million integers with `foldl (+) 0 xs`. Why does this happen and what's the idiomatic fix?
evals.expected_output: Explains that lazy foldl builds a large thunk chain (space leak) because it doesn't evaluate the accumulator as it goes; fix is foldl' (strict left fold). Bonus: general strictness awareness — strict fields, modify' over modify, BangPatterns.
assertions: Explains the lazy foldl thunk buildup / space leak (accumulator not forced as it goes)
Recommends foldl' (the strict left fold) as the fix
Bonus: connects to broader strictness practice (strict fields, modify', BangPatterns)

evals.name: extensions-default-vs-per-file
evals.prompt: To avoid pragma boilerplate, can I just dump all the GHC extensions my team likes into `default-extensions` in the cabal file? We want OverloadedStrings, TemplateHaskell, and GeneralizedNewtypeDeriving available everywhere.
evals.expected_output: Advises against a broad default-extensions list; prefer per-file {-# LANGUAGE #-} pragmas so each extension's effect is localized and auditable. Keep only a small conservative always-on set (DeriveGeneric, DerivingStrategies, LambdaCase, ScopedTypeVariables). Specifically keep risky/situational ones (OverloadedStrings, TemplateHaskell, GeneralizedNewtypeDeriving) per-file. Bonus: rationale.
assertions: Advises against a broad default-extensions list; prefers per-file LANGUAGE pragmas
Names the small conservative always-on set (DeriveGeneric, DerivingStrategies, LambdaCase, ScopedTypeVariables)
Specifically cautions that risky/situational extensions (OverloadedStrings, TemplateHaskell, GeneralizedNewtypeDeriving) should be per-file, not global
Bonus: gives the rationale (localized, auditable effect per module)
